text: Alexander reformed the courts, the army, local government, and on March the 13th, 1881, he
approved a plan that could have been Russia's first step towards an elected assembly.
That same afternoon, revolutionaries threw a bomb at his carriage.
It missed.
Alexander stepped out to check on the wounded, and a second bomber threw another right at
his feet.
The Tsar who freed the serfs killed the day he tried to give people a voice.
His son tore up the plan.
The loop was back on its old setting, and the Tsar after that would be the last one.
So look back at the whole story.
The Slavs invited the Vikings because of chaos.
Moscow learned total control from the Mongols.
The time of troubles gave Russia the Romanovs.
The fall of the Tsars gave Russia Lenin and Stalin.
And the chaos of the 90s gave Russia Putin.
1100 years. Different hats?
Same story.
Will Russia ever break the loop?
Nobody knows. Maybe not even the Russians.
And if you thought Russia's rulers were rough on their own families, wait until you meet the Ottomans.
Their sultans had a law that let them kill their own brothers! See you there!
